items.title: Anthropic steers Claude Code away from recreating specific existing video games; official status disputed
items.summary: Several outlets report that Claude Code now refuses to rebuild or clone a specific existing video game, even with changed mechanics or a new name. Kotaku reports the rule arrived around Oct 27 via a server-side flag with no user setting to turn it off. Game Developer says Anthropic confirmed an update to steer Claude Code away from recreating someone else's specific game, while Tech Insider says Anthropic has not publicly confirmed it as official policy.
items.why_it_matters: A visible case of a lab restricting a coding agent's use case server-side, which hits the game-preservation and decompilation community. Whether Anthropic formally owns the policy is unsettled.

items.title: AgiBot puts six Genie G2 robots on a 24-hour convenience-store shift livestream from Nov 2
items.original_title: 智元精灵G2便利店24小时上岗直播
items.summary: AgiBot (智元) scheduled six Genie G2 robots to run a continuous 24-hour real-store shift from 10:00 UTC+8 on Nov 2, the last stop of its 'AI WAVE' series. They run its Genie Master embodied-agent framework, released Oct 27. AgiBot says task success rose from 28.6% on day one to a stable 85.7% after day five in an earlier store trial; this is AgiBot's own unverified figure.
items.why_it_matters: A public real-world stress test of a Chinese embodied-agent stack, with a result likely to be reported Nov 3.

learn.title: Put an error bar on a success rate before comparing agents
learn.why_today: AgiBot's own figure of task success rising from 28.6% to 85.7% is a before/after comparison of two rates, and the item gives no trial counts.
learn.explanation: A success rate k/n is an estimate of a true rate p, and its uncertainty depends on n far more than on k. The Wilson score interval inverts the normal approximation to a binomial test and, unlike the naive p ± z·sqrt(p(1-p)/n), stays inside [0,1] and behaves at small n or extreme p. With few trials the intervals for two rates can overlap heavily, so a before/after jump is weak evidence; the same percentages from ten times as many trials are far tighter. It still assumes independent trials of equal difficulty, which an agent run in one store over several days violates. The numbers below are illustrative (2/7 and 6/7 happen to give the quoted percentages), not AgiBot's actual counts.
learn.math: \hat p = k/n,\quad \text{CI} = \frac{\hat p + \frac{z^2}{2n} \pm z\sqrt{\frac{\hat p(1-\hat p)}{n} + \frac{z^2}{4n^2}}}{1 + z^2/n}
learn.python:
from math import sqrt
def wilson(k, n, z=1.96):
    p = k / n
    d = 1 + z * z / n
    c = (p + z * z / (2 * n)) / d
    h = z * sqrt(p * (1 - p) / n + z * z / (4 * n * n)) / d
    return c - h, c + h
for k, n in [(2, 7), (6, 7), (60, 70)]:
    lo, hi = wilson(k, n)
    print(f"{k}/{n} = {k/n:.1%}  95% CI [{lo:.1%}, {hi:.1%}]")
